*** BRENT ROLL — STILL HAS NOT ROLLED, ON EXPIRY DAY ITSELF ***
@LCO.1 still reads "ICE Brent Crude (Nov'26)" at 19:08 BST, expiration_date 2026-09-30, settleDate
2026-09-29 at 102.59. So the front month has not switched even on its own expiry date. What HAS
changed since this morning is the spread: Dec'26 rallied 2.19% to 98.27 while Nov'26 rose 1.00% to
103.62, narrowing the gap from $6.98 this morning to $5.35 now. The step-down when CNBC switches is
therefore smaller than it was at 07:36 but still material.
>>> CHECK @LCO.1's `name` FIELD BEFORE THE MORNING BRIEF ON 1 OCTOBER. When it reads Dec'26 the
>>> ticker will show a fall of roughly $5 that is A CONTRACT CHANGE, NOT A PRICE FALL.

*** GILT ADJUDICATION — CNBC's previous_day_closing REJECTED, SIXTH TIME THIS WEEK ***
CNBC gave Tuesday's 10-year close as 5.4147% at 07:36 this morning and as 5.4303% at 19:08 tonight.
Two different values for the same settled close, from the same provider, on the same day. On the
evening figure today's move would be +0.008pp; on the morning figure +0.023pp.
INDEPENDENT ADJUDICATOR — Trading Economics, page updated 202609301800 (18:00 BST today), data only:
  "The yield on United Kingdom 10Y Bond Yield rose to 5.44% on September 30, 2026, marking a 0.05
   percentage points increase from the previous session." TEChartsMeta last = 5.4374.
  That implies Tuesday's close was about 5.387%, and it is coherent with our own 07:36 reading of
  5.382% — i.e. the gilt was roughly flat this morning and has risen through the afternoon.
CORROBORATION — the same pattern appears on the 30-year, independently: Trading Economics has it
"rose to 5.96%... marking a 0.04 percentage points increase", where CNBC's prev of 5.9523% would give
only +0.0085pp. Two maturities, same direction of error, so this is CNBC's prev field being revised
upward across the gilt curve rather than a one-off.
DECISION: publish the gilt at 5.44 with a change of +0.05, on the Trading Economics basis. It is
independently sourced, it is confirmed by the 30-year, and it is the only basis consistent with the
5.38 this site published at 07:54 this morning. CNBC's level (5.438%) is accepted; only its prev is
rejected.

THE DAY'S SHAPE — A REVERSAL OF THIS MORNING. Yields eased overnight and then turned hard: the
ten-year gilt fell to 5.3381% before running to 5.4434%, which Trading Economics records as the
highest since July 2007, and the thirty-year touched 5.9703%. The US ten-year did the same thing,
low 5.201% to a high of 5.306% that is its highest of the year (CNBC yrhidate 09/30/26), finishing
at 5.302%. Gold reached 4,218.16 intraday, a fresh 52-week high (CNBC yrhidate 09/30/26), and then reversed to close near its low
at 4,149.00, down 0.76% — a sharp turn off a record. The FTSE gave up a 10,725.31 high to finish
0.29% lower. Sterling firmed to 1.3263 in spite of the gilt move, which is the notable divergence:
UK fiscal stress usually takes the currency down with the bond, and it did not today.
